segments.summary: Project detection, registry selector, tier merge, runner, coordination lifecycle, and error feed reviewed; abnormal cleanup and parsing bounds are the principal gap.
Optional manager, validator placement/timing, tier checks, GUI readiness, quality review, and hook ordering reviewed; readiness and failure oracles are incomplete.
Canonical coordination projection, lifecycle, hooks, adapters, handoff parsing, and remediation reviewed; fail-safe and retry terminal semantics remain open.
Continuity, safe hooks, availability, parallel dependency groups, worktrees, selection, and UI example evidence reviewed; partial failure and rollback are absent.
Registry validation, invocation, dependency inheritance, coordination ownership, and durable crew-board boundaries reviewed; conflicts and durable-message governance are incomplete.
Projection/message split, schema, routing, rate limits, lifecycle, canonical mechanisms, and provider bridge reviewed; authorization and distributed-state rules are missing.
Cross-worktree awareness, prompt/scenario evidence, platform projection, data model, registration, and partial status API reviewed; idempotency and schema evolution are open.
CAS status mutation, terminal cleanup, prompt aggregation, stale pruning, mirror save, and duration formatting reviewed; one-hour versus two-hour staleness is contradictory.

cross_document_questions: Which canonical owner defines crew-message authentication, authorization, retention, redaction, deletion, and offline reconciliation?
Which runtime contract resolves the one-hour versus two-hour stale-agent threshold and defines the heartbeat/expiry oracle?
Which executor or worktree owner defines dependency-cycle rejection, group cancellation, merge conflicts, cleanup, and rollback after partial parallel failure?
Which GUI owner supplies a falsifiable replacement for the `GUI updated?` readiness criterion, including accessibility and misleading-state checks?
